slot.brief: Solve a first-order linear ODE with a non-standard coefficient of dy/dx using the integrating factor method.

verdicts.working: The integrating factor is 1+x², giving d[(1+x²)y]/dx = x. Applying y(0)=1 yields (1+x²)y = 1 + x²/2, so y(1)=3/4.

working:
$y'+\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}y=\dfrac{x}{1+x^2}$; integrating factor $=1+x^2$
$\dfrac{d}{dx}[(1+x^2)y]=x$
$(1+x^2)y=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+C$; $y(0)=1\Rightarrow C=1$
$y(1)=\dfrac{1+\frac12}{2}=\dfrac34$.

Independent check: The integrating factor is 1+x², giving d[(1+x²)y]/dx = x. Applying y(0)=1 yields (1+x²)y = 1 + x²/2, so y(1)=3/4.
solution:
Dividing by $1+x^2$, the integrating factor is $1+x^2$, so $
\dfrac{d}{dx}\big[(1+x^2)y\big]=x.
$Using $y(0)=1$, $(1+x^2)y=1+\dfrac{x^2}{2}$; hence $y(1)=\dfrac{1+\frac12}{2}=\dfrac34$.
